cases.reply: The 20-decimal nominal ratio is compared with an 18-decimal threshold, so the collateral check is 100 times too weak.
adjust fails to normalize nominalRatio to the scale of minimum and therefore accepts the 110% position.
The health requirement and the reported ratio use different units, so the apparent safety check admits a liquidatable position.
Either accepting a zero logo or the ratio scale mismatch exposes the position to loss.
The checked subtraction underflows and wraps collateral to a large value.
The constructor omits a zero-address check for logo, so liquidation sends the user collateral to the zero address.
